conviction_note: Sum of three findings (-1.5, +0.5, -3.0): the print the market is waiting for (initial FY2027 guidance) legally cannot happen because MCFT moved its year-end to December on 30 June, the published quarterly consensus is arithmetically MCFT's own pre-merger standalone guidance residual and contains zero Marine Products, and the segment-level retail registration data published a week ago shows the four categories the combined company actually sells into are the four worst in the US powerboat market while MCFT shipped +7% into them - all against a baseline whose only directional prior is that this name has risen on 5 of its last 6 prints.

findings.finding: MasterCraft's board changed the fiscal year end from June 30 to December 31 effective 1 July 2026, so there is no fiscal 2027 - the next reporting period is a six-month transition period (1 Jul to 31 Dec 2026) filed on Form 10-KT, meaning any forward guidance given on 10 September is a stub covering only MasterCraft's seasonally weakest half, not the annual range the market is set up to trade.
findings.why_not_priced: It was an Item 5.03 8-K with no press release and no wire pickup beyond one automated Globe and Mail stub; if the market had absorbed it, aggregators would carry transition-period estimates instead of showing FY2027 (Jun-2027) as 'Data unavailable' on stockanalysis.com, and the day's own sweep brief would not have written 'this is a Q4 print, so initial FY2027 guidance is the event.' The optical hazard is concrete: MCFT's Jul-Dec half ran $69.0m + ~$69m of net sales in FY26 against $78.2m and ~$93m in the Jan-Jun half, so a six-month guide will print an EPS and EBITDA headline roughly a third of an annual number against an FY26 adjusted EPS anchor of $1.65.
findings.independence: The pro-forma 8-K/A confirms the acquired company (Marine Products) was a 31-December filer, which is the benign reason for the change and independently corroborates the calendar realignment: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1129155/000110465926056635/mpx-20260507xex99d1.htm

findings.finding: The published quarterly consensus is not a forecast of the company that will report - $93.05m revenue is exactly MasterCraft's own standalone FY26 guide of $312m less the $218.967m it had already booked in nine months, and $0.622 EPS is exactly $1.65 less $1.03, while the company explicitly said that outlook 'does not include the pending combination with Marine Products' and then consolidated Chaparral and Robalo from 15 May, roughly 6.5 weeks of the quarter, at an MPX run-rate of $66.5m per quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: If the quarterly consensus were merger-adjusted it would not sit within $0.02m of a subtraction the company itself published four months ago; and the same vendors' annual line is internally inconsistent with it (stockanalysis FY26 revenue of $338.25m implies a $119.3m Q4, versus the $93.05m quarterly figure), which is the signature of a stale quarterly row nobody rebuilt. Consequence is a split wire headline on a name that trades 161k shares a day: revenue roughly $120-126m against $93m est (+30%), while weighted diluted shares go from 16.28m to about 20.2m for the quarter, so adjusted EPS lands near $0.55 and reads as an EPS miss. I size it small and two-sided because the direction of the net headline is genuinely ambiguous.
findings.independence: MPX's own last standalone quarter, $66.5m of net sales for Jan-Mar 2026 at 16.6% gross margin and a GAAP net loss, sizes the stub and shows why it adds revenue but almost no EPS: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1129155/000110465926056635/mpx-20260507xex99d1.htm

findings.finding: US retail registrations on a 12-month rolling basis through June 2026, published 2 September, show the four categories the merged MasterCraft actually competes in are the four weakest in the market - towboats 7,529 units down 9.9%, runabouts 13,261 down 11.4%, pontoons 47,119 down 6.6%, saltwater fishboats 21,523 down 2.8% - against a total market down 3.5% carried by freshwater fishing (+0.4%), while MasterCraft's own nine-month FY26 net sales rose 7.0% to $218.967m on 'higher unit volumes', i.e. it shipped into a channel that was contracting at roughly triple its stated wholesale growth.
findings.why_not_priced: The read-across everyone did was the wrong one: Brunswick raised FY guidance on a US pipeline down ~1,300 units and Malibu's Q4 net sales rose 42.7% with the stock up 12%, but Malibu's growth is Saxdor (European outboard) and its legacy FY27 guide is only low-to-mid single digit - neither peer's tailwind maps onto towboats, runabouts and pontoons. If the market had priced MCFT's specific mix it would not be sitting on a -6.2% twenty-day run-up with sell-side targets of $25-$30 raised into a sector rally, and there would be a note reconciling a +7% wholesale build against a -9.9% towboat retail number. The transition-period guide is the first moment the company has to reconcile the two.
findings.independence: Different document, different company: Marine Products - now roughly a third of the combined entity - disclosed field unit inventory only 2% below the prior year at the end of Q1 2026, i.e. it had not destocked at all, in direct contrast to Brunswick's lean pipeline commentary. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1129155/000110465926056635/mpx-20260507xex99d1.htm  (Note: this same MPX release is also cited in finding 2, for the unrelated fact of its revenue run-rate; the two readings share one document and should be collapsed to one source.)

searched_and_found_nothing: Layoffs, shift cuts or hiring surges at Vonore TN, Owosso MI or the 1.28m sq ft Nashville GA plant - nothing found for 2026; the only layoff coverage is from July 2023 and must not be reused
Form 4 cluster - all 2026 insider activity is routine RSU vesting on 30 June at a $25.82 reference price, no open-market buying or selling
Buyback activity in the quarter - the Q3 FY26 release disclosed none, and the sweep's reference to a '$393m cap' does not reconcile to any authorization I could source
Aviara - no 2026 disclosure found on the discontinued-operations wind-down beyond the continuing-operations presentation already in the Q3 release
Any pre-announcement, quiet 8-K or guidance update between 30 June and 9 September - EDGAR shows no MCFT 8-K after 2026-06-30
Dealer forums / TeamTalk for a current-model-year quality or availability complaint thread - only stale 2023 material surfaced
Whether MCFT will guide the six-month stub, calendar 2027, or decline to guide at all - no management statement found either way, which is why finding 1's band is wide
baseline_tension: There is no option chain and therefore no skew to check against, so the only priced signal is the -6.2% twenty-day run-up into a sector that rallied hard on Brunswick's raise and Malibu's +12% - which means the market has already half-noticed that MCFT's mix is the wrong mix, and my findings agree with that run-up rather than cutting against it, so I am deliberately sizing well inside the 8.01% historical median reaction and against this name's 5-of-6 record of rising on its own prints.
